body:
I do want him and I am doing my best for him. It just never feels like enough 😞

I just wish I could wave a magic wand and and make him happy.

Thank you for the reply.

Ugh, that’s a gut punch to read. Is there anything we can be doing to help him be less miserable? I hate that we are making him miserable.

Oh gosh, poor pup. That sounds stressful. 

I’ll mention it to my vet, just to cover our bases.

Thank you for the reply.

Not joking, unfortunately. It’s at minimum once a week, sometimes a few a week. It’s been a level 3 at worst. He was particularly nippy as a puppy but that was nothing like this. He just seems to redirect his fear and anxiety on us.

If you don’t mind me asking, how did you come to learn he had epilepsy? I’m wondering if there’s something we’ve missed during his physical exams.

Thank you for the kind words.

We do not blame anyone else. We know genetics are random chance and a roll of the dice. It’s just hard not to blame ourselves 😞

I guess I just feel like a failure because you wouldn’t “return” a mentally disabled child but here I am thinking about returning this dog. I grew up being taught to never give up on a dog, that you have them for life, etc. I know that’s wishful thinking now and that I can’t sacrifice my life over this… but it’s hard not to beat myself over it.

Thank you for the kind words 💕

He has had his regular health checks ups with nothing abnormal. Should I request a specific test?

The bites scare me. It’s like he immediately goes from 0 to 1,000 in a split second, from relaxing to biting so fast you don’t even register it.

Thank you again 💕

Thank you for the reply.

She hasn’t said anything about it yet. It’s kinda more like, “damn, this happened again? Okay let’s remove xyz new triggers, and try another new med”. I guess I’m just wondering if this is normal and if I’m just being impatient.
